open_decision: The order of the new entries inside the appended tail (and whether a starter appears once or more than once) is not fixed by any law.
input: enable = false, locked = (fun _ => false), registry = [], starter list = [{id:1, adapter:1, model:1, enabled:true}, {id:2, adapter:2, model:2, enabled:true}] (distinct ids, both absent)
result_a: [{id:1, adapter:1, model:1, enabled:false}, {id:2, adapter:2, model:2, enabled:false}] (starter order, as ref does)
result_b: [{id:2, adapter:2, model:2, enabled:false}, {id:1, adapter:1, model:1, enabled:false}] (reverse starter order)
reason: Both designs keep the registry rows, append only a tail, add every absent starter once, and set enabled by the rule, so they pass every law. NewAtEnd, AddsOnlyAbsent and AddsEveryAbsent talk about membership of the tail only, so the tail order is free.
